title: Adaptive Page Orchestrator: stateful circuit breakers, regional load-shedding, and automated runbook runner
creator: Marisa Chen
description:
Goal: Reduce noisy pages during multiregion SLO burn while ensuring rapid, deterministic remediation for true outages. Deliver a runtime-side "adaptive page orchestrator" that combines: (a) stateful circuit breakers scoped to logical request groups, (b) region-aware load-shedding that prioritizes tail-latency SLOs, and (c) an automated runbook runner that augments on-call pages with contextual remediation steps and one-click mitigations.

Background: We have recurring noisy pages when a single region experiences transient kernel contention or degraded external dependencies. Current alert rules are too sensitive to SLO burn spikes and lack context for cross-region routing/fallback. Engineers are repeatedly paged for transient degradations that would be solved by automatic regional fallback or temporary shedding.

Non-goals: This ticket does not change customer-facing routing policies (that is separate) and does not implement long-term capacity planning. It focuses on page volume reduction + safe automatic mitigations for low-severity degradations.

Design summary: 
- Stateful circuit breakers (SCB): a small in-memory+durable state machine keyed by logical "request shard" (model_id + customer_tier + route_hash). State persisted to a fast store (Redis primary, fallback to local disk) and replicated across region control-plane instances. States: CLOSED, OPEN, HALF_OPEN. Transitions governed by sliding-window error-rate and slow-p90/p99 latency signals. 
- CB policy: open when error_rate > 5% AND p99 latency > 3x baseline over a 120s window OR sustained CPU/GPU saturation > 90% for 30s. Cooldown: initial open 60s, exponential backoff up to 15m. Half-open: allow 5% of traffic for 30s to test recovery.
- Regional load-shedding: token-bucket admission at per-GPU-group level that consults the SCB state. When SCB for a shard is OPEN in a region, that region rejects non-critical priority requests and routes to fallback region(s) using the smart-routing policy. Shedding decisions consider customer_tier and function: free-tier inference requests are shed before paid-tier evaluation.
- Pager gating & alert tuning: introduce a composite alert "page_orch_slo_burn" that triggers an automated playflow instead of immediate page if the condition is localized (single-region) and total affected QPS < 5% of global load for that model. If the composite evaluates to true for > 2m and traffic fallback fails, escalate to on-call. Add a suppression window (default 3m) that dedups identical fingerprints, tagged by shard + region + root-cause-category.
- Automated runbook runner: when composite fires, we run an orchestration that gathers context: recent SLO graphs, CPU/GPU utilization, kernel/queue backlog, last 10 requests fingerprints, and suggested mitigations (restart worker, flip model variant, apply quantized fallback). The orchestrator exposes a one-click mitigation (e.g., enable-fallback-route) and records actions to incident timeline.

API/Config: New runtime config blocks: 
- page_orch.policy: JSON driven, supports per-model overrides, thresholds, tiers, fallbacks. 
- cb.store.config: redis_url, persistence_latency_SLO, replication_strategy.

Acceptance criteria: 
1) Pager volume for model-level SLO alerts reduced by >= 60% for transient noise windows (measured on canary traffic).
2) All mitigations are auditable in incident timeline and reversible via console.
3) No customer-visible increase in 95th percentile tail latency for paid-tier customers beyond 5% from baseline.
4) Automated runbook runner successfully executes at least two mitigation actions in staging and writes audit events to the incidents service.

Testing & rollout plan: 
- Unit tests for SCB transitions and persistence. Integration tests that simulate region failure and assert proper shedding/reroute. Chaos test via staged CPU/GPU contention in staging clusters.
- Canary rollout: 1% traffic on dedicated canary region, monitor SLO dashboard for 48h. If stable, expand to 10% and then 50%.

Metrics to monitor: p99 latency, error rate, SLO burn (1h / 6h), pages per fingerprint per region, number of automatic mitigations, false positive rate of composite alert. Dashboards: https://grafana.redwood.com/d/ops/slo-dashboard?view=page-orch

Docs & Runbooks: design doc: https://confluence.redwood.com/display/RI/Page-Orchestrator-Design. Implementation PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/8123. Runbook (live): https://runbooks.redwood.com/page-orchestrator.

Open design trade-offs and questions: 
- Persistence: Redis provides low latency but introduces cross-region consistency concerns. We will accept eventual consistency for CB state, and rely on conservative open intervals to reduce oscillation.
- Visibility vs suppression: aggressive suppression reduces noisy pages but can delay wake-up for real incidents. We mitigate by requiring composite conditions (latency+errors+utilization) before suppressing pages.
- Who can configure shedding rules: default rules will be runtime-managed; tenant-specific overrides require RBAC review.

Next steps: 
- Implement SCB state machine (PR #8123) → in review.
- Integrate runbook-runner hooks into paging pipeline (work in progress).
- Prepare canary cluster and dashboards for the rollout.
